sections.t: Where she lives and how she is reached
sections.x:
- She is one person in several places: the Keeper's window on his laptop (widow.html, installed as a small app), the Tower and the game wherever the Keeper calls her, and a full-screen TV view of the same window (the TV button) that can be cast to a television: Chrome or Edge menu > Cast, or Windows + K for a Roku or smart TV.
- In her window he can type, hold the microphone button (or the Space bar) to talk, or turn on "Listen for Widow" so she answers whenever he says her name. "New talk" starts a fresh page; "Look again" reads the world again; "Sign out" closes her.
- In the game he holds Z (or the right grip in a headset, or her microphone button on her card) and begins with "Widow".

- What he asks her to keep, and their recent talk, are kept on the server for the Keeper alone, so she remembers it in her window, in the game and on the TV alike. If that store has not been switched on yet, her window keeps them on the laptop instead.

- In her window she reads the world as the Keeper, only to look: who is walking Somnucor, the dreamers, the Keeper's inbox, orders, gold waiting to be exchanged, the city treasury, the job board, applications, shifts, wages paid, safety reports, today's Gazette, and the Keeper's switches for cameras, drones, lights and events. She looks again every few minutes while her window is open.
- She knows the game from her handbook: the features, the Tower guide, what came after, and where every Keeper control is.

- She cannot change anything in the game yet; the Keeper names each power before she has it.
- Files: she may save a text file into the one folder he picked on his laptop ("Pick her folder"), and read files already there. She shows the file first and saves only on his yes.
- Email: she writes the email and shows it; on his word, his own mail program opens with it ready to send (or, if he connects his Gmail in "Email setup", she sends it herself).
- Errands: on his word she opens a website, looks something up on Google, plays a song or video on YouTube, shows a place on a map, calls a phone number through his phone program, or opens the game or the Keeper's Desk. If the browser holds the new tab back, she offers a one-click Open button.
- Outside questions: she looks up what she is unsure of on Wikipedia. She cannot see live news, weather or prices.
- She speaks up on her own when something needs him: a new letter in the Keeper's inbox, gold waiting, a safety report. With "Alerts" on, she also taps his screen with a notification when her window is hidden.
- She runs on the same AI the game uses, through the game's own relay; no other service and no extra subscription.
26 October 2026 · Thaddeus

SomnuMatrix (the Dream Walker's Atlas) is a finished, live 3D online world built by one person. It starts from a dream journal: speak or type a dream and walk through it. From there, players step into a shared living city, a full K-12 school, a prompt-to-3D Simulation Studio and a universe of 41 travelable worlds. It plays in the web browser on PC, Android phones and Meta Quest 2, with no install, and has been live since 7 October 2026 with seven paying players.

| At a glance |  |
| --- | --- |
| Core | A dream journal that builds each dream as a walkable 3D place |
| Prompt to 3D | The Simulation Studio: type or speak a scenario and walk through it as a training site (12 kinds of building, 5 drills) |
| Shared city | Somnucor, a real-time society: jobs, gold, bank, police, courts, homes, family life and a working city crew |
| Living people | Every person in the city holds a real, unscripted conversation, remembers you on every device, has their own personality and a voice that fits their age and sex, and uses a phone |
| School | One K-12 school: 105 courses, 3,150 lessons, an AI teacher in every classroom, grades, transcripts and a full school day |
| Worlds | 41 travelable worlds, 29 with a great city of their own, plus hidden worlds |

| Story worlds | 43 classic stories, the Odyssey, 16 Shakespeare plays, Leonardo's Italy, Jules Verne's world, the Grimm Wood, Erebos, the Deep, the Labyrinth and Samhain Night each autumn |
| Buildings | Every building in every world can be entered, with an inside that fits what it is and where it stands |
| Play styles | Life sim, exploration, hunts, crafting with an optional skill tree, racing, magic, PvP battle (18+) |
| Devices | PC, Android phones, Meta Quest 2 (VR, controllers and hand tracking) |
| Admin | The Keeper's Desk: one console for players, prices, events, danger levels, the school, the city's people and every hidden treasure |

In one line: RuneScape meets Second Life meets The Sims, built around your own dreams.

Every dream a player tells becomes a 3D place they can walk through, built at once and offline.

- Speak or type. Tell the dream out loud or type it, night by night.
- Instant build, offline. A catalogue of about 54,000 words builds the dream on the device straight away.
- Fills the gaps. For anything the catalogue does not know, an online design step reads the whole night, looks names up on Wikipedia and Wiktionary, and designs what is missing.
- Layered dreams. Where things stand in relation to each other ("fishing on a small boat in deep water") is understood, so the pieces fit together.
- Dreams that move. Trees sway, water flows, clocks keep the dream's hour; pieces include treehouses, submarines, gingerbread houses and black holes.
- Dreamt buildings open. Buildings dreamt up in the journal can be entered, with insides that fit what they are.
- Dream powers. Flying, walking on water, breathing underwater, becoming unseen, changing shape, summoning, stopping time, blinking, changing size, speaking with the dead, lucid dreaming, changing the dream by naming a thing, seeing what was hidden, and healing, each with its own effect.
- Private by default. The journal stays on the player's device, with an encrypted vault.

- Share a dream as a world. One button turns a night into a world other players can visit; the written words go only if the dreamer ticks the box. Dream creators can earn from visits.
- Dream lands. Dreams can cross into sixteen dream lands (the Underworld, the Heavens, the Depths, Faerie, the Void, the Mirror World, the Land of the Dead, the Frozen Realm and more), each fully dressed with places, people who talk in character, and real facts.
- Memory book and photo mode. Keep favourite moments as pictures in a personal memory book.

Type or speak a scenario and walk through it at once as a simulated training environment. The same engine that turns a written dream into a world turns plain words into a complete, enterable building, for corporate training and architectural simulation. It opens from Menu > Simulation.

- Say it, walk it. "A warehouse with three forklifts and a fire exit drill" or "a two-storey office floor plan with meeting rooms" becomes a whole site in moments: the building, its car park, rooms, stairs, lift and fire exits. Every door opens and every floor is there.
- 12 kinds of building. Warehouses, factories, shop floors, data centres, offices, hospitals, schools, hotels, laboratories, restaurants, houses and construction sites. The words set the floors, the size in metres or square feet, the cladding, and what is inside (forklifts, racking, desks, beds, machines, checkouts and more).
- 5 training drills. Fire evacuation (raise the alarm, avoid smoke and blocked exits, never the lift, report to the fire warden at the assembly point), forklift safety with working forklifts that stop and sound their horn, a hazard hunt, a first aid response and a spill response. Each ends with a result card and is kept as a training record.
- For architects. A training board in every building gives the size, the floor area and a floor plan showing where you are, the ways out and the assembly point.

- Save and share. Scenarios are kept on the device, and a share link opens the same building for anyone.
- Everywhere. Walkable on a computer, a phone or a Quest 2. The words are read on the device, so a building appears at once; the city's AI can add a fuller layout when it is reachable.
- Keeper control. On or off; open to everyone, to members only or to the Keeper only; AI layout on or off; the Keeper's own example scenarios.

Every person a player meets in the city holds a real conversation, made fresh each time, never read from a script.

- True conversation. Each visit starts a new talk, and even the first words are the person's own, in character. Replies never repeat; if the AI is slow or busy, the person tries again rather than falling back on a stock line.
- Every person is unique. Every resident has their own name (no two share one), job, home, daily life and fixed personality, with opinions of their own built from their job, world and name.
- Age and sex match. How old a person is comes from how they look (grey hair older, children 7 to 12), and how they speak fits their age. Men and women have matching voices; children sound higher and quicker, older people slower. People never announce their age, sex or memories unprompted.
- They remember you. Each person keeps a short memory of every player they have met: how often, when last, and what was said or promised. It follows the player from PC to phone to headset.
- They know who you are. Every person knows a player's name and whether they are the Keeper (met with respect, never fawning), a dues-paying citizen or a visitor.

- They speak aloud. People speak their replies out loud and answer a player's own voice with a Hold to talk button, face to face or by phone. A speaker button by Send turns voices on or off, with a Settings switch for the city's people speaking out loud.
- Phones. People order from businesses, call for repairs and text each other; players can text anyone they have met, and businesses text players when an order or a cab is ready. Around town every call is acted on: crimes go to the Dragon Corp (a rider is sent and a statement taken), homes order deliveries that are taken, packed and delivered, repairs go to the trades, and major emergencies (fire, flood, power cut, a ship aground, a mine collapse) ring the Keeper, who is asked what to do.
- Phone calls. Voice calls between dreamers ring anywhere in the game (Phone > Messages > a dreamer > Call), with Answer, Decline, Mute and Hang up; 18+, with blocking. Dreamers can also ring the city's people (Phone > Town > a person > Call), who answer aloud in a voice that fits their sex and age, and the people they know can ring them, speaking first; missed calls are kept in Town, with a Settings switch and a Keeper switch.

- A city that runs. Bin lorries on their rounds, street sweepers, the postie, the night watchman, delivery vans that arrive at the right door, road works, and building sites that grow over real days. Workers can be talked to.
- Players' own free key. Paying players add their own free AI key within seven days of buying. It is free, takes about two minutes and is strongly encouraged: a step-by-step guide opens by itself, with a daily reminder after. Without a key after seven days, the city's people answer with simple lines until one is added. The key stays on the player's device.
- Always free. The deities of Temple Row answer every player, paid or not; the dream journal is unaffected; the Keeper always gets full conversation.

One full K-12 school in Somnucor, with a second campus (the Commons School), runs by itself until real teachers take the posts. It teaches a standards-aligned, openly licensed curriculum.

| Part | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| Courses | 105 courses from Kindergarten to Grade 12, one classroom per subject per grade, including Spanish and computer science from Grade 6 |
| Lessons | 3,150 full lessons; each unit has an overview, three lessons and a unit quiz (pass at 80%), every grade written at its own reading level |
| Teachers | "Ask the teacher" in every classroom and lesson book: an AI teacher who gives hints, not answers; players without a key are still taught from the book |
| School day | Morning meeting, 45-minute lessons, recess, lunch and clubs, with soft bells |
| Electives | Art studio, music room with a playable keyboard, drama club in the auditorium; all on the report card |
| Records | Standards codes on every unit, course tests, first-try scores, letter grades and GPA, attendance and an hours log, enrolment, a timetable and a printable transcript |
| Staff | Counselor, nurse, principal, librarian and a Director of World Learning, each to talk to |
| Families | "My class" shows a teacher or parent their pupils; the teacher and parent lock keeps out every live player the grown-up has not allowed |

| Sources | Openly licensed for commercial use: Project Gutenberg, PhET, OpenStax and Wikibooks |

The school's learning also reaches the worlds: the Odyssey voyage teaches the real places, the science and the words at every stop, and many worlds hold their own lessons.

College partners. Online colleges list their courses inside the game (Menu > Places > College courses, and College courses buttons at the school's front office, library, atrium and report card). A player who picks a course goes to the college's own page with a referral code, then enrols and pays at the college. The college reports each student as enrolled, completed or refunded, through a simple partner-key web call or by email. The Keeper's share is set per college (10% by default).

Somnucor is one city every player shares in real time, built to work the way real life works. Only dues-paying citizens hold jobs, live there and earn gold; visitors can explore.

Work and money

- Real jobs with real 8-hour shifts and wages, across shops, works, offices, temples, the hospital, police, courts, the school, the Underground and more; jobs depend on each other as they would in reality.
- Apply on site at any workplace with an opening, or through the hiring boards; promotions and raises.
- Open a business with a permit from the Tower, run a market stall, stock a warehouse, and restyle your own building inside and out.
- A gold economy with the Bank of Somnucor (accounts, safe-deposit vault, mortgages), a city treasury and a mint.
- Bills like real life: hospital, insurance, power and water, by letter to your mailbox, with brokers for insurance. Nobody is gaoled over a bill.
- Errands: every person you talk to, and every other player or business, can post errands to run for pay.

Law and order

- Police, a gaol and full court trials (judge, counsel, jury, witnesses), with assault, theft and crime reports.
- The law of the road: traffic lights, speed limits, crossings, tickets; city drivers are trained and also under the law.
- Driving and flying licences, with a learner car and a driving test.

Getting around

- The Transport Yard car dealership with sales staff and test drives; your own cars, bikes, carriages, mounts and flyers.
- City cabs you can call to any address; ride with friends, family cars, company carpools and a lift pass.
- The Underground railway: buy a ticket from the clerk at the booking office and ride it, or take a job and drive the train with real signals. The Underground also runs to the World Mall.
- A helicopter flies from any helipad to the World Mall's roof.
- Realistic first-person cockpits for every vehicle; in a vehicle only its own controls show.
- Working vehicle lights on everything that moves: headlights that light the road after dark, brake lights, turn signals and reversing lamps on cars; lanterns on coaches; navigation lights on ships; wing lights and a slow beacon on aircraft. City traffic signals at the kerb and brakes at stops. One key (L) switches between automatic and always on.
- Street racing at night (8:30 pm to 5:30 am city time), with a race finder on the compass.

Daily life

- Needs: health, food, drink, energy and hygiene; sickness and cures at the Apothecary; the City Hospital with duty nurse and doctor; falls hurt.
- Homes to buy or rent, furnish, decorate with your own pictures and signs, and extend with 17 kinds of room and 5 grand additions from Hearth & Beam Builders; rest and washing work in every home.

- A home vault that holds anything you own, safe from loss.
- Home guests: whoever lives in a home can let other dreamers in, always or for 3 hours, take them off again, or hold an open house for 1 or 3 hours, from Menu > Guests and kitchen. It covers every home they live in, World Bundle houses included, and respects blocks and the teacher and parent lock. Visitors at a locked door can knock, which sends the resident a phone message.
- Stocked kitchens: the Bakery, Greengrocer's, Butcher's, Dairy, General Store and Brewhouse sell 37 grocery packs to take home in a shopping bag (a loaf is 8 slices, a dozen eggs is 12). At home, players put shopping away in the fridge, freezer and cupboards, eat and drink from them, and cook 12 meals at the stove, from eggs on toast to roast chicken and spaghetti bolognese. Guests may eat from the kitchen.
- Your own door in the Hall of Doors, decorated from the start (stone arch, oak planks, lanterns, brass nameplate, knocker), which dreamers can restyle, with rare frames and ornaments unlocked by rare materials they hold.
- Family life: marriage and weddings, fostering and adoption, children who need room and care.
- Pets and mounts; 36 Dreamskin Atelier skins; base, trim and accent dyes on every piece of clothing, gear and mount.

- World Bundles (18+, $29.99 each): themed packs, each a house with two secrets on a shared street in its world, plus a pet, an outfit, a mount with a war power and 1,000 gold. Three so far: the Underdark (a manor hanging from the cavern roof with a wyvern perch), Jules Verne's world (an engineer's lighthouse on the shore) and Leonardo's Italy (a Tuscan villa with gardens). The owner's name is on the door, and only the owner and the Keeper can go in.

Places to go

- The World Mall: three floors round a domed atrium, 40 units where real outside stores open a shop and sell real products.
- The Dreamers' Book Store: three floors, 20 kinds of book each in its own room, a café, author corner and children's room; players list their real books and buyers follow a link to the real store.
- The Picture House cinema (five screens), the library, concerts and dance clubs, party rooms, the Pixel Palace arcade.
- Temple Row: about 275 deities, each with an enterable temple in one of 14 styles, who answer in character.
- Two magic academies with tuition (see Magic).

Together

- World chat and local chat, voice chat, ten emotes, who's here, follow a friend.
- Guilds, arenas and reputation, levels, ranks, goals and leaderboards.
- Chess, draughts and poker with other players.

- Keeper-made events, parades and holidays that players can join with floats; the Gazette, breaking news and a "Tonight in Somnucor" board; weather that matters, city projects and market prices.
- SomnuMatrix Live Views on Roku: the Keeper places cameras in safe, public outdoor places (Menu > Place a Roku camera here), and a Roku channel shows a grid of near-live pictures, refreshed about every 15 seconds; OK opens one full screen. Players' names and chat are hidden, and cameras are never placed indoors, in homes or in private dreams.

Beyond the city lie 41 travelable worlds, and 29 of them have a great city of their own, each made to fit its world. Every world has something to do: work, trade, gathering, a game, a lesson and somewhere to stay, listed on its "Things to do" board. Every world has its own music and sound.

| Group | Worlds | Highlights |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dream lands | 16 lands, including the Underworld, the Heavens, the Depths, Faerie, the Void, the Mirror World, the Land of the Dead and the Frozen Realm | Each fully dressed, with people who talk in character and real facts |
| Space | The Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Pluto, four cloud stations at Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, Station Aurora, the Ares Gateway, open space | Shuttles and the Orbital Line; laser tag and laser-sword duels on Station Aurora |
| Jubilee, the Party Planet | Always night under a ringed giant and two moons | Festival field, beach, glamping lodges; built for big live events |
| Ironfray (18+) | The battle world | Anything-goes PvP and beasts, war machines, forges, gold for victories |
| Pyreline | The race planet | The whole planet is one racetrack: climates, shortcuts, falling roads, last car standing; entry by recommendation from the Street Racing Club; about 50 cars to earn |
| The Greenwold | Gardens, orchards, fields and farm | Kept by Mother Nature, who talks live in character |

| The Guildlands | The crafting world | Always safe; home of the optional skill tree |
| The Kids Zone (Wonderglen, in Faerie) | Always safe | Zoo, circus show, a colouring area with our own pages, puzzles, games and stories, in bold bright colours |
| GiGi's Lounge and the Family houses | Calm places to gather | Always safe |
| The Hall of Doors | The doorway to the grand story worlds | All 24 doors dressed as their own world, with lettered name plates and gilt mirrors between them; coming back puts you right in front of the door you used |
| Underground and World Mall | Worlds of their own | Work, trade, games and lessons |

Hidden worlds must be discovered; the ways in are never shown on any map: Neverland, the Endless Sea and its islands, the Underdark (a dark-elf city of great Houses in giant stalactites, a Dwarven Deep, glowing fungus and the Sunless Sea), the North Pole (Santa's village, the Palace of the North King, volunteer work for the elves that earns one-of-a-kind gifts), the Hidden Crescent casino on the Moon (18+, with baccarat, craps and blackjack wings), and Veyar.

Great cities. Through a gate in each world stands its own city: a palace on two terraces, eight great houses (schools, guilds, temples, markets, libraries, hospitals, banks, courts, theatres and more), a training ground with a timed drill, homes, and a far district of mines, works and farms. Every building is bigger inside than out, with 8 to 12 furnished rooms, staff who talk in character, a hiring desk, daily lectures with quizzes, and an exchange desk for the city's goods.

Mines that grow. Miners dig their mine deeper with every shift, opening twelve new parts in turn, down to a great cavern that everyone can see.

Every building opens. Every building in every world has a door and an inside that matches what it is and where it stands: a castle has a great hall, throne room and towers; a temple its own sanctuary; an igloo, a crypt, a lighthouse and a skyscraper each their own kind of rooms. That covers the dream lands, Shakespeare's London and Stratford, Leonardo's Italy, Jules Verne's world (down to the Paris Opera), Samhain Night and every story world, each inside furnished for its story's own time and place. The fairy castle in Faerie alone has 65 rooms on three floors. Insides are built only when you walk in, so phones stay quick. The few deliberate exceptions are Lilliput's tiny houses, Rapunzel's doorless tower, and a handful of houses standing in water.

sections.t: Story worlds and grand figure worlds
sections.x:
Great stories and great lives are played, not just read: each gets a world you can walk through, chapter by chapter. All are public-domain sources retold in our own words, never copied from any film.

The Voyage Home (the Odyssey). All sixteen chapters of the Odyssey played across the islands of the Sunless Sea, in three boats you can borrow: the Cyclops, the Sirens, Lady Circe's island (where careless sailors may join her menagerie) and the rest. A star marks every chapter where you did better than Odysseus.

The Labyrinth. One endless, living maze that fills a whole world, always changing, stone and hedge growing through each other, with ten halls from every age of history and a deeper level beneath. At its deepest, most hidden point lies the Heart: the first dreamer to reach it becomes Master of the Labyrinth and controls it (turning the maze, a full map, beasts that ignore them) until someone else gets there. The Keeper can never hold it.

sections.t: Story worlds and grand figure worlds
sections.x:
43 classic stories. Each has a story board in the world it fits, with its people to talk to, and a grand world of its own about 2 km across, played chapter by chapter at great landmarks. Daily gold rewards, a keepsake for finishing, and 118 costumes of the main characters to buy. The stories include Alice in Wonderland, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, Treasure Island, Dracula, Frankenstein, Robin Hood, The Sword in the Stone, Beowulf, Gilgamesh, The Arabian Nights, Journey to the West, Pinocchio, The Snow Queen, The Little Mermaid, Sherlock Holmes, Don Quixote, Gulliver's Travels, The Time Machine, The War of the Worlds, The Lost World, Sleepy Hollow, Norse and Greek myths, Egyptian and Irish legends, and Japanese yokai tales.

Shakespeare's London. London in 1600 and Stratford-upon-Avon, with every building enterable, including the Globe. Sixteen plays are played act by act, each in its own world: Hamlet, Macbeth, King Lear, Othello, Romeo and Juliet, A Midsummer Night's Dream, The Tempest, Twelfth Night, As You Like It, Much Ado About Nothing, The Merchant of Venice, Julius Caesar, Antony and Cleopatra, Henry V, Richard III and The Winter's Tale. A library of the plays, sonnets, words and Shakespeare's life; character costumes; safe everywhere; one hidden find.

sections.t: Story worlds and grand figure worlds
sections.x:
Leonardo's Italy. Florence, Leonardo's workshop, a flying hill and proving ground with his machines you can ride, Vinci, Milan (the Last Supper and the Great Horse), Amboise, and Romagna, the only dangerous part. Mirror-writing notebooks and puzzles, lessons, painting at an easel, a Master's exam, its own gear, and one hidden find.

Jules Verne's world. An 1870 Exposition harbour and Paris; Around the World in Eighty Days as a weekly race with a leaderboard; a guided tour of the Nautilus; The Mysterious Island and the Journey to the Centre of the Earth as grand adventures; the Moon gun, a balloon over Africa, the Albatross airship, Verne's library, lessons, inventors' benches, and one hidden find.

The Grimm Wood. Kassel in 1812, with the Grimms' house and the inn where Dorothea Viehmann tells her tales, then a great old German wood with sixteen tales played in their own clearings and a winter corner. The tales are told as the Grimms' book has them, dark endings included, for grown readers, not as a children's area. The complete book (208 tales) can be read inside. 92 doors, each opening onto a room of its own kind, and one hidden find.

sections.t: Story worlds and grand figure worlds
sections.x:
Erebos, the Greek Underworld. A large world beneath the Underworld dream land, reached by its eastern path or Charon's ferry: the Vestibule and the Elm of False Dreams, the Acheron and Charon, Cerberus at the gate, the judges, the Fields of Asphodel, the palace of Hades and Persephone, Lethe, the Styx, the Phlegethon, the House of Night, the Cave of Sleep, the Gates of Horn and Ivory, Tartarus with its famous prisoners, Elysium and the Isles of the Blessed, and Orpheus's path. 20 enterable buildings, 12 lessons and one hidden find. Safe in most places; the burning river is Dangerous and Tartarus is Deadly.

The Deep. The dream land under the sea, built as two great places. Hans Christian Andersen's mermaid kingdom: the Sea King's palace (44 rooms on two floors), the princesses' gardens, two shell towns and the Sea Witch's wood. Plato's Atlantis: the rings of land and water, the temple, the palace, baths, the racecourse, ship sheds and triremes. Every building opens with undersea insides; 10 story shells, 10 tablets to find, and dolphins to ride.

sections.t: Story worlds and grand figure worlds
sections.x: Samhain Night (each autumn). A seasonal Halloween world through a gate on the city plaza or the Hall of Doors: a village with old Samhain customs, a bonfire hill, the Headless Horseman's ride to the chapel bridge, Ravensmoor House (13 and over, a timed escape), Pumpkin Hollow for younger players (friendly ghosts, a corn maze, a candy trail, carving and a puppet theatre), and a drive-in cinema (18 and over). One hidden find. The Keeper sets the dates, the music, the pay and what plays on each screen.

sections.t: Magic, gear, mounts and mythic machines
sections.x:
Every ability matters: each spell, charm and power works against every kind of enemy, other players and creatures alike.

Magic academies

- The Academy of the Arcane on Temple Row: a castle with moving staircases, a Great Hall with floating candles, galleries, a library and dungeons; lessons with lore cards, rune practice and a question.
- The Somnucor academy's Spellwright Wing and Academy Grounds: Blink, Mirror Double, Darksight, Polymorph, Starfall, Starlight Wisp and more, practised on a casting range.
- Duskwell, the dark academy deep in the Underdark: eight dangerous dark spells (shadow and illusion, curses and hexes, fear, lore of the dead, silk and venom) across a teaching floor, a students' floor with an alchemy laboratory, and a Deep Floor with a proving cavern.
- Tuition in gold, paid to the city treasury (Somnucor 250, Duskwell 400 by default, set by the Keeper); under-18s study free unless the Keeper changes it.
- A spellbook and a powers bar; keys 1 to 0 on PC, buttons on phones, controllers in VR.

Weapons, armour and gear

- Swords, axes, maces and daggers that swing and spark, shields, guns, horns, spell shots and orbs.
- Every world sells its own gear: 264 pieces across 39 worlds (weapons, armour, a mount and two charms per world), never repeated between worlds.

sections.t: Magic, gear, mounts and mythic machines
sections.x:
- The forges: players make weapons, armour, cars and war machines, with recipes that show the exact amount of each material.
- The crafts: an optional levelled skill tree for gathering and crafting, shown only to dreamers who take it up: 12 crafts, levels 1 to 60 and five tiers of tools.
- 48 elemental relics across six elements, plus the North King's eleven ice relics.
- 24 rare artifacts, one of each in the universe, never sold, at most one hidden in any world.
- Rare materials (star crystal, emberstone, dragon scale, elemental essences, deepsilver and more) are found only, never sold.

Mounts and vehicles

- Pets and mounts, a mount for every world, dragons, cars with neon and metallic finishes, carriages, airships, saucers and about 50 race cars on Pyreline.

Mythic machines

- One of each, hidden across the universe, never sold, each with three powers and a full pilot's cockpit: the Brass Widow (eight-legged steam walker), the Corsair Kestrel (light freighter), the Twinvane Shrike (fighter), Ashvaal the Pearl Domeship and the Ironhide Bulwark (heavy tank).
- Six beast mechs (Rosehorn, Nightwyrm, Emberwing, Frostfang, Riddlecrown and Blazehorn) lock together into one giant mech, the Sovereign, crewed by their pilots.
- A holder can send a machine back into hiding for others to find.

Every world has a danger level set by the Keeper, so players always know what they risk.

| Level | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| 0 Safe | No fighting. The city, your own dream, the Greenwold, Jubilee, the Kids Zone, stations, the casino, the World Mall, the Heavens, the Hall of Doors, the North Pole, GiGi's Lounge, the Family houses, Shakespeare's London, the Guildlands and the Simulation Studio are always safe |
| 1 Guarded | Fights only when both agree (a challenge and an accept) |
| 2 Risky | Open fighting outdoors |
| 3 Dangerous | The winner takes 5% of the loser's purse (up to 250 gold) and a special item may drop; beasts may ambush you |
| 4 Deadly | The winner takes 10% (up to 1,000 gold) and a drop; beasts may ambush you |

- In PvP, the winner takes the special relics and artifacts the loser was carrying; anything kept in a home vault is safe.
- Ironfray (18+) is open battle: PvP and beasts, with gold for victories. Fight music comes in during any battle.

Hunts and treasures

- The Dreamer's Keys: a seasonal great hunt with three keys in worlds beyond the city (Copper: a riddle; Jade: a race through waymarks; Crystal: a duel with a guardian). The first citizen through the Gate of Dreams wins the season's gold prize, the Dreamer's Crown and a Gazette story. Key places and riddles rotate each season.

- Golden Invitations: exactly 20 printed invitations, each opening once and giving a numbered keepsake ("No. N of 20") that can never be sold, traded or given.
- Hidden finds: at most one hidden relic or artifact in any world, plus the mythic machines; found only, never sold.
- Rare things register: a public record of rare items and their holders, with offers between players.
- Seasonal: Santa at the North Pole, played live by the Keeper, with wish lists and gifts.

The Backpack

Everything a player gains goes into the Backpack, sorted into tabs, and can be moved to the home vault for safekeeping.

Every world has its own sound, all made by the game as it plays, so there are no recordings to license.

- Three themes per world, with ambience fitted to where you are, including inside buildings.
- Fight music for nine seconds after any blow, shot, spell or blast, in the worlds that need it.
- Stages, clubs, films and Samhain Night keep their own music; sound dips while someone speaks.
- Volumes in Settings; phones and headsets get a lighter mix.
- The Keeper can turn music or sounds off per world, or add a chosen track for any world.

sections.t: The Keeper's Desk, accounts and safety
sections.x:
The owner (the Keeper) runs the whole game from one admin console, with no code needed.

Keeper controls

- Players, citizenship and dues; grants and roles; chat moderation and reports from the in-game bug button.
- Prices and the catalogue; the money desk; the gold exchange rate; academy tuition; daily gold for stories and plays.
- Events, parades and holidays; the Gazette; Santa's season.
- Danger levels for every world.
- The World Mall: store sign-up, a store portal, an embeddable store widget and partner feeds; picture house and bank spaces granted to tenants.
- The Dreamers' Book Store: approve each book and link before it goes on a shelf.
- Every hidden treasure: relics, artifacts, mythic machines, Golden Invitations, the Dreamer's Keys season, and the Master of the Labyrinth (view or clear).

sections.t: The Keeper's Desk, accounts and safety
sections.x:
- A panel each for the City School (opening, closing, hiding), the college partners (colleges and courses, share, partner keys, reports by date, printable monthly statements and payments received), home guests and kitchens (switches, limits, stock or empty a kitchen, grocery prices), the Roku cameras, the Simulation Studio, the living people, the living city, players' own keys (who has one, days left, give seven more days), music and sound, the World Bundles, Shakespeare's London, Leonardo's Italy, the classic stories, the Grimm Wood, Erebos, Samhain Night, the crafts and the dreamers' doors.
- The Keeper plays for free, can never be ticketed or charged, and never wins the hunts.

Accounts and payments

- Membership: $29.99 once, for life. Gold: 100 gold for $1. World Bundles: $29.99 each.
- Sign-in with two-factor protection; every database table locked with row-level security.
- One-time purchase through Stripe Checkout, set up by pasting a payment link and signing secret into the console.
- Real-money gold is optional, off by default, and 18+ only.

Safety

- Age checks enforced by the server: under 13 refused; 18+ for voice chat, phone calls between players, real-money gold, World Bundles, the casino and Ironfray.
- Moderated chat, blocking and reporting; account deletion.

sections.t: The Keeper's Desk, accounts and safety
sections.x:
- A teacher and parent lock: the same game with no other live players except those the grown-up allows.
- No strobing or flashing anywhere, checked on every change; nothing blinding.

One game runs in the browser on all three devices, with no app store and no install.

| Device | What it gets |
| --- | --- |
| PC | Full detail: photographed real surfaces, detailed bodies and vehicles, keyboard and mouse or gamepad |
| Android phones | A light mode built for phones (about 85% of players), touch controls, worlds released from memory when you leave them, a calm recovery card if the graphics give out |
| Meta Quest 2 | Full VR through the headset's browser, controllers and hand tracking, cockpits drawn at true depth |

Built with HTML and JavaScript, three.js, WebXR, Supabase (PostgreSQL, two-factor sign-in, row-level security, server functions), Stripe Checkout and browser speech. Worlds are built on the device, a few hundred KB each; school lessons load one course at a time. An animated loading page (aurora, shooting stars and a dream-city skyline) keeps a smooth bar moving while each world builds.

sections.b: The Helix Tower — where everything is, and every Keeper control

sections.b: The Helix Tower — where everything is, and every Keeper control
sections.x:
- The periodic floor — all 118 elements lit in their families' colours, laid out as a floor you walk across.
  Stand on one and press E: its number, mass, configuration, shells drawn as a diagram, what it is, and a
  button for live figures from PubChem (melting and boiling points, density, electronegativity, who found it).
- The reaction benches — ten real reactions run step by step, with what you see, the balanced equation,
  why it happens, and a question. The beaker in front of you changes as you go.
- The practical benches — six practicals done by hand: lighting a Bunsen burner, weighing out a solution,
  a titration with real burette readings, water of crystallisation, the heating curve of water, growing
  copper sulfate crystals. You pick what to do at each step; a wrong pick is explained, never punished.
- The flame test burner — seven metals, each with its colour and its brightest line, and the line spectra
  on the wall behind.
- Study room 1 — ten lessons with questions. Study room 2 — the equation balancer and the molar mass
  calculator (type any formula, brackets and water of crystallisation included).
- The Elements Cabinet — twelve real samples behind glass.
- The Compound Library — any compound, live from PubChem.
- Your progress — elements read, reactions run, lessons passed, your rank.

sections.b: The Helix Tower — where everything is, and every Keeper control
sections.x:
- The helix hall — a great double helix of light turning slowly, with the story of how the shape was found.
- The teaching benches — six practicals: onion cells, your own cheek cells, a heart dissection, a flower
  dissection, DNA from strawberries, and a gel run that asks whose DNA it is.
- The Strand Reader — real genes read through RNA into protein by the real codon table, and the whole table.
- The Punnett square — cross two parents and see the chances.
- The Gene Library — any human gene, live from Ensembl.
- Genetics lessons and your progress, as on the chemistry floor.
- Behind glass: sequencing, the copying room, cell culture, the cryogenic biobank, bioinformatics.

sections.b: The Helix Tower — where everything is, and every Keeper control
sections.x:
A training drill, and it says so the whole way: an invented illness, six doors to seal, three people to find
and walk out, four waves of drill targets stopped with marker rounds, and the real lesson as you go — R,
incubation, isolation, tracing, protective kit, decontamination in the right order. Danger 3; adults who pay
dues and hold a level 3 card; you may always go and are never hurt. Fire with E or F or a click.
Beaten, you wake at the way in, as with the beasts.

sections.b: The Helix Tower — where everything is, and every Keeper control
sections.x:
- Heard by all inside the Tower: announcements, spoken and written at the top. Her lines are made fresh,
  so they never repeat.
- Talked with by anyone carrying a card, her depth following its level.
- The wake word: hold the talk button and begin with "Widow", anywhere in the Tower. In a headset that is
  the right grip; on a keyboard hold Z; on a phone it is the Hold to talk button on her card.
- Her terminals: the lobby, every floor by the lifts, the Research Facility, and her Heart at the middle
  of the Web (level 5).
- Your systems report: open her and press the button. It shows the AI connection, your own key, the model,
  her memory, her last error, which floors are open and whether the exercise is running.
- She is the same character as your own Widow window, word for word, so she is one person wherever you meet her.

sections.t: The rule that is kept everywhere
sections.x:
Nothing explosive, ever. Anything energetic is named "unstable" and nothing more — no composition, no amount,
no step — and the library holds no agents of war. Grey fever, the illness in the drill, is invented. The check
tests both of these.
